messages:
Maya Chen: FYI pushed a small routing change to prefer local POP for short seq (<128) requests — seeing odd p95 delta between us-east/us-west/eu-west. Posting charts: https://redir.example/reports/1920012345
Samir Patel: looking now. rough numbers?
Maya Chen: p50 pretty stable across regions (~18-22ms on H100 pool), but p95 in eu-west jumped from ~90ms -> 145ms after the change. us-west p95 up ~30ms. us-east almost unchanged. attaching span heatmaps.
perf-bot: auto-summary: H100-a100-mix cluster
- us-east: p50 20ms p95 78ms
- us-west: p50 21ms p95 112ms
- eu-west: p50 22ms p95 145ms
Devon Lee: do we have routing logs? might be falling back to remote kernel or proxy hop.
Maya Chen: yes, example trace id: trace_2026_1920012345
Span shows extra proxy hop when edge route chooses 'fallback-tier' DNAT -> proxy-eu-backup.
Elena García: hmm did the kernel negotiation pick a quantized path there? eu hosts are still on quantized-llama-q4f16 kernel for LLM-2-7B trial.
Samir Patel: good call. if eu is on q4f16 kernel and local POP can't satisfy batch size, we might be spawning on a remote compatible host. check kernel_count by region.
Maya Chen: query I ran:
```
SELECT region,kernel,avg(p95_latency) FROM routing_spans WHERE trace=1920012345 GROUP BY region,kernel
```
Results: eu-west -> q4f16 avg p95 140ms; us-west -> q5_og avg p95 110ms; us-east -> q5_og avg p95 76ms
Ravi Kapoor: capacity note: eu-west GPU pool is 60% reserved, autoscaler slow (scale-up cooldown 120s). If routing prefers local POP but local pool saturated, fallback creates cross-pop hop.
Devon Lee: can we force route policy to prefer remote same-region instead of fallback-tier for short seq to avoid proxying? or increase concurrency threshold so local accepts smaller batches.
Maya Chen: temp mitigation: reverted the route change for short seq at edge. Will test toggling kernel preference too.
Elena García: also run eval on quality — q4f16 has slight compaction artifacts for this prompt family; maybe quality tradeoff causing different model runtimes -> slower kv cache hits.
Samir Patel: action items:
- Maya: revert is live, monitor p95 across pops for 20m
- Ravi: raise eu-west scale-up aggressiveness for next hour
- Devon: run kernel compatibility sweep to ensure quant kernels don't force remote exec
- Elena: run a small eval set to compare q4f16 vs q5_og output quality for these prompts
Maya Chen: noted. initial quick check after revert: perf-bot posted new metrics -> eu-west p95 down to 92ms after 4 minutes, us-west 98ms.
perf-bot: update at +4m: us-east p95 78ms, us-west p95 99ms, eu-west p95 92ms. no errors.
Ravi Kapoor: I'll still queue a burst request to verify scale-up works; will report back in thread.
Devon Lee: thanks. if this stabilizes we should add a routing test to CI that simulates kernel mismatch + pool saturation to avoid regressions.
Maya Chen: agreed — will open a quick PR with a smoke test harness. cc @perf-bot for dashboards.
Samir Patel: thanks all. Short follow-up: please paste any traces where proxy hop >1 and label them so I can find persistent bad actors.
Maya Chen: will do. closing this thread for now, will reopen if p95 climbs again or kernel sweep shows regression.
